title: PreAccident Podcast Thematic Index
description: A public machine-readable index of ranked PreAccident Podcast episodes across seven safety themes.

episodes.title: PAPod 571 - Fail Fast, Learn Faster: A Conversation on Human Performance and Recovery
episodes.evidence: The title centers Human Performance, and the description states that human error is normal, context shapes behavior, and system recovery matters more than blame.

episodes.title: PAPood 563 - Human Performance, Not Human Error — Todd Conklin on Reframing Safety
episodes.evidence: The description directly frames HOP and safety as products of complex systems rather than individual mistakes.

episodes.title: PAPod 582 - Accountability vs. Blame: Who Really Owns Safety?
episodes.evidence: The title and description directly distinguish accountability from blame, discipline, and performance management while defining shared responsibility before incidents.

episodes.title: PAPod 175 - Just Culture: The Movie - Sidney Dekker's Interview on the Documentary
episodes.evidence: The description defines restorative Just Culture through trust, forward-looking accountability, repair of harm, and movement away from blame and punitive responses.

episodes.title: PAPod 66 - A Discussion on Human Error
episodes.evidence: The description states that human error is normal, noncausal, misunderstood, and misused in safety learning and corrective action.

episodes.title: PAPod 566 - Blame Stops Improvement: How Blame Silences Learning
episodes.evidence: The title and description make blame the central issue, linking it to misunderstood human error, silenced learning, and the choice between asking what failed and who failed.

episodes.title: PAPod 489 - A Deep-diving Conversation with Sidney Decker
episodes.evidence: The description centers forgiveness, blame, accountability, and organizational learning, presenting forgiveness as a mechanism for learning after failure.

episodes.title: PAPod 569 - PART TWO: 11 Seconds: How a System, Not a Nurse, Failed
episodes.evidence: The description explains a medication error through normalized overrides, software defaults, and organizational assumptions, then addresses criminalization and the shift from blame to system-focused learning.

episodes.title: PAPod 568 - PART ONE:  Charged for a Mistake: The Nurse, the Error, and a System That Failed
episodes.evidence: The description provides a context-rich account of a medication error, including system conditions, workarounds, interruptions, decision points, and criminal charges.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Accountability Counts
episodes.evidence: The description challenges accountability used as a weapon against workers and reframes it around creating conditions in which workers can succeed.

episodes.title: PAPod 493 - A 20 Year Look Back at Fundamentals of Human Performance
episodes.evidence: The episode centers the origins and evolution of Human Performance and explicitly discusses blame culture and accountability as a group effort.

episodes.title: PAPod Special - Honoring a Safety Pioneer: James Reason's Legacy
episodes.evidence: The description reviews James Reason's work on human error in complex systems and his development of Just Culture.

episodes.title: PAPod 496 - A Deep Dive into a Energy Company's Resilience with Christian Gould
episodes.evidence: The description centers HOP, explains why it must be adapted to cultural and operational context, and addresses the pitfalls of blame culture.

episodes.title: PAPod 114 - Johan Bergstrom on Human Error for Humans
episodes.evidence: The title centers human error, and the description reframes error as normal and no longer independently informative within Safety Differently.

episodes.title: PAPod 159 - Risk-Based Thinking - A new book by Tony Muschara
episodes.evidence: The description states that the episode is entirely about managing operational uncertainty arising from human error through Human and Organizational Performance thinking.

episodes.title: PAPod 12 - Meet my first Human Performance instructor
episodes.evidence: The description directly states that worker errors are normal and that most errors are operationally unimportant.

episodes.title: PAPod 602 - From Brazil with Safety: Gilval and the New View Revolution

episodes.title: PAPod 45 - David Marx - The Just Culture Guru Has a New Book!
episodes.evidence: The title identifies Just Culture as the central subject, while the description focuses on choice, free will, and New View safety and operations.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Humans are more comfortable with culpability then chaos

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Sidney Dekker on Why Things Go Wrong

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Why you can't have it both ways.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - How We React - Matters (a lot)

episodes.title: Safety Moment - What Leadership Sounds Like...

episodes.title: PAPod 16 - Bob Edwards - The HOP Coach

episodes.title: PAPod 42 - Safety Differently - Daniel Hummerdal

episodes.title: PAPod 27 - Safety Differently - A conversation with Corrie Pitzer

episodes.evidence: The title directly frames the episode around safety, resilience, and COVID-19, but the description is boilerplate.

episodes.title: PAPod 302 - Healthcare Safety in the Time of Covid19 - Meet Dr. Stephen Jones - Yale New Haven Health System
episodes.evidence: The title directly concerns healthcare safety during COVID-19, making pandemic operations the apparent context, but no substantive description is available.

episodes.title: Corona Virus: A Nation in Paradox - Opening Schools in the Time of Covid19
episodes.evidence: The title centers the operational paradox of reopening schools during COVID-19, but the generic series description provides limited thematic depth.

episodes.title: PAPood 563 - Human Performance, Not Human Error — Todd Conklin on Reframing Safety
episodes.evidence: Complex-system emergence, organizational capacity, and resilient operations receive substantial record-specific treatment, although Human and Organizational Performance and human error remain the dominant frame.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - A Better Definition of Risk
episodes.evidence: The episode directly reframes risk through variability, complexity, nonlinearity, instability, and worker uncertainty, but risk definition remains the principal subject.

episodes.title: PAPod 140- Two Tragic Stories about Controls, Resilience, and Recovery - The Great Bill Rigot
episodes.evidence: Recovery and limiting consequences after serious failure are central, but controls and consequence management are the primary mechanisms.

episodes.title: PAPod 565 - Fear, FOMO & Fixing Safety: A Conversation with Brent Sutton
episodes.evidence: Safe-to-fail experiments, weak signals, resilient systems, and evolving workplace complexity are substantive, though innovation and leadership responsibility remain prominent.

episodes.title: PAPod 583 - When Normal Variability Breaks: The ReDonda Story
episodes.evidence: The record explicitly explains serious failure as an interaction of normal performance variability, but the dominant purpose is workshop promotion and post-event learning.

episodes.title: PAPod 550 - Bent but Not Broken: Navigating The Nexus Between Social and Organizational Resilience
episodes.evidence: Social and organizational resilience, adaptation, and systems under pressure are explicit, but the episode primarily concerns a personal story, fear, leadership response, and culture.

episodes.title: PAPod 588 - Weak Signals, Big Consequences: The RaDonda Story
episodes.evidence: Interacting performance variability and resilience across complex systems are directly supported, although the episode primarily promotes a restorative workshop and event learning.

episodes.title: PAPod 532 - Lessons from Leadership with Doug Parker and Jim Frederick
episodes.evidence: The description addresses how the COVID-19 pandemic reshaped OSHA operations and required adaptation to uncertainty, but leadership, governance, enforcement, and compliance dominate.

episodes.title: PAPod 32 - Fatalities and Serious Events:  A New View - Jim Howe
episodes.evidence: Systems thinking and the framing of serious events as operational failures are meaningful, but fatalities, event distinctions, prevention assumptions, and management response are primary.

themes.theme_name: Risk, Controls, Procedures, and Operational Assurance

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Essential Safety Controls
episodes.evidence: The record explains a start-work approach that identifies essential controls and requires their validation and verification before work begins.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - A Progressive Method of Workplace Safety
episodes.evidence: The record develops the STKY method from identifying the highest-consequence risk through identifying essential controls and testing whether those controls are sufficient.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Vital Relationship Between Risk and Control
episodes.evidence: The episode explicitly argues that risk identification is insufficient unless matched with effective controls, barriers, safeguards, and mitigation within the operating system.

episodes.title: PAPod 581- Measuring the Invisible: When 'Nothing Happened' Breaks Safety Metrics
episodes.evidence: The episode directly challenges accident-frequency measures and develops better metrics for validating safeguards, leading indicators, and verification practices.

episodes.title: PAPod 37 - Dr. Jim Joy - Critical Controls
episodes.evidence: The title and description center on Critical Control Management and the connection between critical tasks, risk management, and critical controls.

episodes.title: PAPod 492 - An Insightful Conversation with Georgina Poole and Sidney Dekker
episodes.evidence: The description centers on the validity, limitations, manipulation, and organizational use of safety metrics, including TRIR and injury-frequency measures.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Start Strong, Finish Strong: The Power of Effective Job Initiation
episodes.evidence: The episode explains how controls, tailboard meetings, toolbox talks, and critical-thinking preparation at job initiation build capacity for unexpected conditions.

episodes.title: PAPod 598 - What If Risk Never Leaves? Exploring Transportable Hazards
episodes.evidence: The episode distinguishes hazards from dynamic risk and examines risk transfer, controls, barriers, margin, and the conditions for starting work safely.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Power of Independent Verification
episodes.evidence: Independent verification is the central practice, with an additional set of eyes used to detect mistakes and prevent failures before they propagate.

episodes.title: PAPod 11 - Gotta Fix Everything?  Not according to Tony Muschara...Critical Steps
episodes.evidence: The episode develops Critical Steps as a method for concentrating controls on work-process points where failure would have the highest consequences.

episodes.title: PAPod 576 - From Continuous Improvement to Continuous Capacity: 10 Operational Indicators You Need
episodes.evidence: The episode presents a dashboard of measurable operational indicators and explains how regular monitoring links safeguards, engineering controls, and high-risk operations.

episodes.title: PAPod 512 - Picking Up Pennies in Front of a Steamroller: Understanding High Risk and Low Reward
episodes.evidence: The episode directly analyzes high-risk, low-reward work and asks organizations to evaluate risk-reward tradeoffs through operational risk assessment and decision-making.

episodes.title: PAPod 498 - Balancing Adventure and Risk in Outdoor Education
episodes.evidence: The episode substantively examines outdoor-activity risks, accident-pattern identification, supervision, water hazards, safety precautions, and prospective prevention strategies.

episodes.title: PAPod 186 - Critical Risk Management - This is what it looks like in action...Meet Jennie Bailey
episodes.evidence: The episode is explicitly about critical risk management in practice and the operational relationship between risk, control, and pre-job activity.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Myth of Leading Data: Focus on Action, Not Prediction
episodes.evidence: The episode directly challenges the validity and value of leading data and predictive approaches, contrasting them with action on identified real-world risks.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Why Stop Work May Be A Bad Idea
episodes.evidence: The record critically examines reliance on stop-work policy and argues that it functions only after other organizational safeguards have failed.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Luck Has Nothing To Do With Safety
episodes.evidence: The record replaces explanations based on luck with an explicit evaluation of which safeguards worked and which safeguards failed.

episodes.title: PAPod 577 - Near Misses: The Unexpected Gift That Keeps Workers Safe
episodes.evidence: Near misses are used specifically to determine whether controls functioned or luck prevented harm, making safeguard performance the principal learning question.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Success of Failure?
episodes.evidence: The central decision is whether an event represents safety failure or safeguard success, requiring managers to evaluate control performance with limited information.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Cardinal Rules are not so Cardinal
episodes.evidence: The record challenges cardinal rules as a reliability mechanism and proposes managing the associated controls rather than assuming rule compliance prevents accidents.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Stop Work Authority is a Prevention Tool NOT a Barrier
episodes.evidence: The record evaluates stop-work authority as a prevention practice rather than a control or barrier and explains the operational consequences of treating it otherwise.

episodes.title: PAPod 111 - How Manager's Should Think About PreJob Briefs
episodes.evidence: The episode directly examines managerial responsibility for making pre-job briefs effective across an organization and questions how the practice should function.

episodes.title: PAPod 84 - Marc Yeston LIVE! at HPRCT
episodes.evidence: The presentation explicitly centers on planning high-risk work as a means of creating operational capacity before execution.

episodes.title: PAPod 603 - Procedures: The Double-Edged Sword of Safety
episodes.evidence: Procedures are the central subject, including their stabilizing and constraining effects in high-risk work and their relationship to flexibility and everyday execution.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Map is Not the Territory: Understanding Procedures in Real Work
episodes.evidence: The record evaluates procedures as stabilizing models that cannot fully represent actual work and explains how workers adapt them to operational variation.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - A Key To Increased Safety
episodes.evidence: The episode examines conflict points where procedures and work systems misalign, including a safety-analysis document that hindered operations and required user feedback.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Rumble Strips
episodes.evidence: Rumble strips are examined as a concrete safeguard and barrier designed to tolerate human variability rather than depend on eliminating error.

episodes.title: PAPod 562 - When 'I Forgot' Becomes Fatal: Preventing Children Left in Hot Cars
episodes.evidence: The episode translates a predictable memory-failure hazard into practical system controls, including technology and visual reminders, to prevent or recover from hot-car events.

episodes.title: PAPod 140- Two Tragic Stories about Controls, Resilience, and Recovery - The Great Bill Rigot
episodes.evidence: The stories are used to examine controls that limit consequences, shifting attention from preventing every event to controlling the next failure's outcome.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Be Prepared
episodes.evidence: The episode directly contrasts ineffective exhortations with preparing for potential events through built-in safeguards and defenses.

episodes.title: PAPod 108 - Not Compliant...but not NOT compliant.  Carsten Busch
episodes.evidence: The episode directly examines compliance as a complex, observer-dependent operational judgment rather than a simple binary condition.

episodes.title: PAPod 341 - Ron Farris, Jim Marinus, and Tony Muschara - How's That for a Great Line Up?  Critical Steps  :Managing What Must Go Right in High-Risk Operations
episodes.evidence: The title directly centers Critical Steps and managing what must go right in high-risk operations, placing control of critical work at the core despite the boilerplate description.

episodes.title: PAPod 342 - Ron Farris, Jim Marinus, and Tony Muschara - How's That for a Great Line Up?  Critical Steps  :Managing What Must Go Right in High-Risk Operations - PART TWO
episodes.evidence: Part Two retains the same direct focus on Critical Steps and managing what must go right in high-risk operations, with thematic strength limited only by the boilerplate description.

episodes.title: PAPod 533 - Exploring the Future with Doug Parker and Jim Frederick
episodes.evidence: The description substantively examines OSHA enforcement and assurance, movement beyond minimum compliance, and proactive health-and-safety management-system practices.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Manny Albert - This Is Why?
episodes.evidence: The record presents a practical method for discussing specific work risks, conditions, and consequences with new workers rather than relying on unexplained rules.

episodes.title: PAPod 511 - The Fox and the Hedgehog: Unraveling Risk Perception
episodes.evidence: The episode develops individual and organizational perspectives on risk perception and applies them to creating a risk-informed, competent workforce.

episodes.title: PAPod 580 - Start Right, End Safe: Building Better Encounters in 2026
episodes.evidence: The record gives job initiation a concrete control function by requiring the right controls before work starts, although culture and psychological safety are competing subjects.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Risk Is Fluid
episodes.evidence: The episode rejects one-time, static risk identification and explains that operational risk changes over time, requiring continuing assessment.

episodes.title: PAPod 171 - TESLA Safety and Lagging Indicators - Let's Hear From Laurie Shelby - Global VP for Health and Safety
episodes.evidence: The record directly questions interpretation of Tesla's lagging injury numbers and the usefulness of backward-looking measures, though it provides limited measurement methodology.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Hazards are Fluid - Those Babies Move!
episodes.evidence: The episode centers on workers discovering changing and previously unrecognized hazards, but does not describe a formal identification or control method.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - The Problem with Plans
episodes.evidence: The record directly tests whether plans, procedures, and prevention are sufficient to produce safe and reliable work, although the treatment is brief.

episodes.title: PAPod 182 - Essential Controls and Fatalities - A beginner's discussion
episodes.evidence: The title directly identifies essential controls and fatalities as the subject, but the boilerplate description provides no record-specific control mechanism.

episodes.title: PAPod 198 - Back By Popular Demand - Steve Scott and Critical Controls -  Don't Miss This Again!
episodes.evidence: Critical controls are explicitly identified as the episode subject, but the description is mainly republication and promotional context rather than substantive control evidence.

episodes.title: PAPod 380 - Is This The Beginning Of The End of TRIR?
episodes.evidence: The title directly questions continued reliance on TRIR, supporting a focused measurement-validity issue despite the absence of substantive description metadata.

episodes.title: PAPod 272 - When Life Saving Rules become Life Threatening Hazards - Nippin Anand talks about his most popular social media post, ever!
episodes.evidence: The title directly examines how life-saving rules can themselves create hazards, but the boilerplate description does not establish the mechanism or examples.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Rules are Just Administrative Controls
episodes.evidence: The title specifically frames rules as administrative controls, but the absence of substantive description metadata limits the supported depth.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Pre-Job Planning Builds CAPACITY!!!
episodes.evidence: The title identifies pre-job planning as a mechanism for building operational capacity, but the description supplies no record-specific planning method.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Why STOP WORK may be the wrong thing to emphasize
episodes.evidence: The title directly questions organizational emphasis on stop-work practice, but boilerplate metadata prevents evaluation of the underlying control argument.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Procedures don't control worker behavior... but worker behavior drives procedural use.
episodes.evidence: The title identifies a specific relationship between worker behavior and procedural use, but the description is entirely boilerplate.

episodes.title: Safety Moment - Procedures are Not Smart Enough to Know Where They Will Fail
episodes.evidence: The title presents a specific limitation of procedures, namely that they cannot identify where they will fail, but no substantive description supports further depth.
